findings.title: UsernameForm calls a no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` that does not exist
findings.description:
`UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only declaration in the tree is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in `UsernamePasswordForm.java:160`, and a grep of `services/src/main/java` finds no other definition or overload in the superclass chain. javac rejects this call, so the `services` module will not build and nothing downstream, including the testsuite, can run.
Fix this together with the helper change below. The most likely intent is a no-arg helper, `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. That signature makes line 47 compile as written.

findings.title: First-login conditional passkeys are disabled, which breaks existing tests
findings.description:
The helper returns `false` whenever `user == null`, and the call sites at `:115` (`authenticate`) and `:137` (`challenge` error path) depend on it. Before the diff, both paths filled passkey data when no user was set. The diff inverts that condition, so the first login page never calls `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm`. That method is the only place that sets `enableWebAuthnConditionalUI` (`WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:43` and `:51`). Without the flag, `login.ftl:16` renders `autocomplete="username"` and the `#webauth` form is not rendered.
The existing test `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, which the diff does not touch, asserts `username webauthn` and the `#webauth` form on that first page (`PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:145-146`). It will fail. The new first-page assertions in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` and `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` (for example line 192) assume the same behavior.
The name is also backwards. The helper returns `false` in exactly the username-less conditional-UI case. `OrganizationAuthenticator.initialChallenge` (`OrganizationAuthenticator.java:357-360`) uses the correct convention and fills when `user == null`.
Suggested fix: make the helper `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with only the `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` check, and update the callers at `:115` and `:137`. The user-dependent decision already lives in `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` (`WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:101`, `:128`), so the helper does not need the user.

findings.title: PasswordForm's error path now shows passkey UI that its first challenge does not
findings.description: `challenge(context, error, field)` now fills passkey data whenever a user is set. `PasswordForm` (constructed with a session at `PasswordForm.java:35-37`) always has a user (`requiresUser()` is true) and overrides `authenticate` (`:45-52`) so it does not fill on the first challenge. A wrong password goes through `badPasswordHandler` and then `challenge(context, msg, FIELD_PASSWORD)` (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:224`), so the re-rendered password page now carries the conditional-UI attributes. No test covers `PasswordForm`. If this is intended, it needs a test and a comment. If not, gate it. This stays true after the helper fix above.

findings.title: Duplicated re-auth flag check and a package cycle
findings.description:
`setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` re-implements `Boolean.parseBoolean(getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH))`. That logic already exists as `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:257-260`), which is still used at `:129`, `:139`, and `:250`. The util cannot call the protected instance method, so the check now lives in two places.
The util also imports a constant from `authenticators.browser` (`AuthenticatorUtils.java:35`), while that package already imports the util (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:24`). That is a package cycle. The constant was made `public` (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58`) only to allow this import, which widens its visibility.
Suggested fix: keep one implementation, for example a static `AuthenticatorUtils` helper that takes the session and is called by both the util and the instance method.

findings.title: Test passes on any exception, not only "element absent"
findings.description:
The same pattern appears at `:312-317`. The block is `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(webauth), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) {}`. The assertion only works because `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is absent. The broad `catch (Exception)` also swallows any other WebDriver failure, such as a stale session or timeout, so the test can pass without proving the element is missing.
Replace it with `Assert.assertTrue(driver.findElements(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")).isEmpty());`. `org.junit.Assert` is already imported in this file.

findings.title: Unused import left behind by the diff
findings.description: The diff removed both `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` uses, so `import org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException;` is now dead. It does not affect behavior. Remove it.

findings.title: Copy-pasted re-authentication test setup across three classes
findings.description: `PasskeysUsernameFormTest` and `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` each contain a near-identical `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` with the same inline passwordless policy block. `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` extracts that block into `setPasswordlessPolicyForExternalKey()` at the end of the file. Move the shared helper into `AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest` so the three copies stay in sync.
